chunks: And from him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, from Ahmad ibn 'Umar, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the time of Dhuhr and 'Asr, so he said: 'The time of Dhuhr is from when the sun begins to decline (shift from zenith) until the shadow (of an object equal to its height) disappears to the length of one shaft's height, and the time of 'Asr is from one shaft's height and a half until two shaft's heights.'

key_terms.الظِّلُّ قَامَةً: A shadow equal to the height of the object (one 'qamah')
key_terms.زَاغَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun declined/shifted from its zenith
key_terms.قَامَتَيْنِ: Two shafts' heights (double the object's height)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific shadow measurements that define the start and end times for Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) provides the foundational juristic criteria for determining prayer times through observable solar phenomena, specifically the transition from shadow length equaling an object's height to double that length. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise temporal boundaries (waqt) derived from natural signs, ensuring the validity of obligatory acts within their prescribed windows.
